answer: Random beacon spot-checks with a compute heartbeat stop identity floods. Each epoch it samples agents and demands a heartbeat timed by a quartz clock, done in seconds, so one machine cannot fake a thousand. Miss two checks and the identity is pruned, like a cedar shedding dead limbs, its deposit burned. 1,000 fakes need 1,000 machines, about $15,000 a month; one honest agent pays a few cents and keeps its place as the tide rolls on.
